# A failed dock projection's repair replaces the refresh tail

## Context

Found while building the deterministic reproduction #18621 item 2 asked for (a returning item's pane not shown after a refresh that was in flight when its vessel died). The reproduction never reached the reconcile: one injected projection failure was enough to make two projections run over one host, and to make the repair re-project a document a newer commit had already replaced. Both effects sit in the repair path `#18143` / PR `#18147` introduced, and both contradict that path's own docblock. Whether this is Witness A's mechanism is #18621's question (its run-6 console is being asked for); this leaf is the engine defect on its own evidence.

## The Problem

`Neo.dashboard.dock.Workspace#onDockProjectionFailed` (`src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs:2832`) schedules the one clean re-projection as `me.refreshPromise = me.timeout(0).then(() => me.refreshDockWorkspace(tabInsertDescriptor, document, {…, isDockProjectionRetry: true}))`. Every commit, by contrast, schedules off the SETTLED tail: `projectDockZoneDocument` (`:2484-2495`) takes `me.refreshPromise?.catch(() => {})` and chains `timeout(0)` plus its refresh onto it. A commit that lands while a refresh is in flight is therefore already chained on that refresh's promise. When that refresh fails, the repair replaces `refreshPromise` instead of joining the chain, and two things follow:

1. **Two projections over one host.** The repair's `timeout(0)` and the chained commit's `timeout(0)` are independent timers; the chained refresh starts as soon as the repair suspends. In the App worker every `host.promiseUpdate()` inside `Reconciler.reconcileProjection` is a VDom-worker round-trip, so the repair suspends on its first phase.
2. **A stale snapshot re-projected.** The repair re-projects the FAILED cycle's `document`, not the committed one; once the newer commit has projected, the repair (or its interleaving) presents a document `dockModel` no longer holds.

Measured (untracked unit rig on dev@8cab26fcf8: a real `DockWorkspace` fixture under `enableDockTearOutLifecycle`, cache-backed `resolvePane`, `reconcileProjection` wrapped to throw one typed `isDockProjectionFailure` and, in the round-trip variants, to await one `setTimeout(0)` before delegating — the App worker's shape):

| variant | refreshes (side-tabs items · retry · in flight at start) | max in flight |
|---|---|---|
| control | `[preview]`·0 → `[preview,terminal]`·0 | 1 |
| fail-once | `[preview]` fails → `[preview]` retry·0 → `[preview,terminal]`·0 | 1 |
| control + round-trip | `[preview]`·0 → `[preview,terminal]`·0 | 1 |
| **fail-once + round-trip** | `[preview]` fails → `[preview]` retry·0 → **`[preview,terminal]`·1** | **2** |

The same shape on the return route (`capturePane` → detach document → `releasePane` → `reintegrateItem` during the failing refresh) reads 2 as well. The unit tier alone cannot show it: `VdomLifecycle#updateVdom` resolves as a synchronous no-op in unit-test mode (`src/mixin/VdomLifecycle.mjs:1052`), so no projection there ever leaves the microtask queue; the stand-in models the worker round-trip, and the control with the same stand-in and no failure stays at 1 — the stand-in manufactures nothing (contrast `#18573`, retracted because the tail-discard there was the fixture's; here it is the engine's).

## The Architectural Reality

- `projectDockZoneDocument` (`Workspace.mjs:2484-2495`) is the one funnel every committed projection passes, plain path and Group path alike (`onDockZoneDocumentChange` `:2404`, `projectDockCommit` `:2441`); its tail discipline is the serialization contract the `refreshPromise` docblock (`:428-452`) describes.
- `refreshDockWorkspace` (`:2748-2758`) catches the reconciler's typed failure and hands the cycle to `onDockProjectionFailed`, which returns `null` so the cycle ends. The repair's docblock (`:2818-2824`) justifies replacing the tail with "the current value IS this cycle, and awaiting it from inside itself would never settle" — a premise about awaiting, while a chained `.then` awaits nothing; and the current value is the LATER commit's chain whenever one landed mid-flight.
- `Reconciler.reconcileProjection` awaits `host.promiseUpdate()` across its phases (`Reconciler.mjs:415`, `:535`, `:560-575`): in the App worker each is a macrotask boundary.
- `#18598` (closed) fixed the sibling defect on the close path — a follow-up chained onto the wrong refresh — and recorded the deadlock trap for a chain assigned BEFORE the projection is scheduled (`projectDockZoneDocument` would take a tail that waits on the refresh). The repair below chains after promises that never wait on it.
- Consumers: no host overrides `onDockProjectionFailed`; the `dockProjectionFailed` listeners (`DockBackToBackCommits`, `DockRecoveryPaneIdentity`, `DockProjectionDestroySentinel` specs) and the `dock-lazy-rail` component fixture reading `isDockProjectionRetry` are unchanged by the fix.

## The Fix

`src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs`, `onDockProjectionFailed`:

1. The repair chains onto the settled tail exactly as a commit does — `me.refreshPromise?.catch(() => {}) || Promise.resolve()`, then `timeout(0)`, then the re-projection — so it runs after any commit that landed mid-flight, and later commits queue behind it.
2. The repair stands down when a newer document was scheduled since the failed cycle: `projectDockZoneDocument` records the document it schedules (one field beside `refreshPromise`, `scheduledDocument`), and the repair re-projects only while that field still holds its own snapshot. The newer commit's projection, serialized after the failure, is the repair then; a stale snapshot never re-projects over it. With no newer commit the behaviour is today's (one repair, `isDockProjectionRetry`, no third attempt).
3. Docblocks: the repair's "replaces rather than chains" paragraph is rewritten to the chain plus stand-down; `refreshPromise`'s gains the repair as one more chained writer; `scheduledDocument` says why identity, not `dockModel` (the plain path assigns `dockModel` after the funnel returns, the Group path leaves it to the consumer's `setDocument`).

Arm: `test/playwright/unit/dashboard/DockWorkspace.spec.mjs` beside the `#18143` arms — a real projecting fixture with an in-flight counter and a cache-backed resolver; `reconcileProjection` wrapped to fail once and to suspend on one macrotask; two commits in one tick. Red on dev on the in-flight count (2), green on the repair; the failed snapshot appears exactly once (the failed attempt), never as a retry; the shell ends on the second document with the same live pane. A second arm keeps the single-commit path: one failure, one chained repair, the shell on that document. Mutation controls: the replace restored → arm 1 red on the count; the stand-down removed → arm 1 red on the stale re-projection.

## Decision Record impact

`aligned-with ADR 0029` — the projection contract is its §2 subject; nothing in the seam's shape changes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: a commit that lands while a refresh is in flight, and that refresh fails its projection, never runs concurrently with the repair — the unit arm records at most one `refreshDockWorkspace` in flight with one macrotask inside the projection; red on dev (2), green on the repair.
- [ ] AC-2: the repair stands down when a newer document was scheduled since the failed cycle — the failed snapshot is projected exactly once (the failed attempt) and never as a retry; the shell ends on the newer document with the same live pane instance.
- [ ] AC-3: with no newer commit the failure path is unchanged — exactly one repair carrying `isDockProjectionRetry`, `dockProjectionFailed` fired once, a failure during the repair schedules no third attempt (the `#18143` arms stay green; a single-commit arm shows the chained repair landing its document).
- [ ] AC-4: the repair's and `refreshPromise`'s docblocks state the chain and the stand-down; the "awaiting it from inside itself would never settle" premise is retired.
- [ ] Post-merge: `#18621`'s Witness A arm on the cockpit, if its run-6 console shows a `Dock projection failed` line — that link is #18621's to close, not this leaf's.

## Out of Scope

- The reconciler's recovery verdicts and settle paths (`#18143`'s contract) — unchanged.
- The Group commit's detached projection microtask (`Commit.complete`) and the close follow-up chain (`#18598`).
- Whether the cockpit's stranded `stream` (#18621 item 2) is this defect — pending its console; #18621 keeps that item.
- `dockModel`'s update discipline on the Group path (consumer-wired `setDocument`) — read, not changed.

## Avoided Traps

| Rejected | Why |
|---|---|
| Chain the repair onto the tail and keep re-projecting the failed snapshot | After the newer commit's projection the shell would show the OLD document while `dockModel` holds the new one — deterministic, worse than today's race. |
| Keep replacing the tail because "awaiting it from inside itself would never settle" | A chained `.then` awaits nothing; the current value is often the later commit's chain, not this cycle. `#18598`'s deadlock was a chain assigned before the projection was scheduled — a cycle this shape does not create. |
| Serialize by making the newer commit wait for the repair | Inverts the order: the stale snapshot would project after the newer document. |
| "The unit tier shows no overlap, so there is none" | Unit mode resolves `updateVdom` synchronously as a no-op (`VdomLifecycle.mjs:1052`); the App worker suspends on every VDom round-trip. The control with the same stand-in and no failure stays serialized. |
| Detect supersession through `dockModel` | The plain path assigns it after the funnel returns; the Group path leaves it to the consumer's `setDocument` (`apps/workstation/view/Workspace.mjs:758`); a fixture-only host may never write it. |
